subject.title: fix(agents): preserve runtime tool inheritance tokens

question: After rebasing this PR, should OpenClaw preserve policy-filtered MCP/LSP runtime selector tokens in spawned child inherited allowlists, or should the fix move closer to runtime materialization instead?
rationale: The branch fixes a real subagent MCP gap, but the permanent boundary controls child-session tool authorization and now overlaps newer policy code on main.

options.title: Refresh and accept selector preservation
options.body: Resolve conflicts against current main and land the existing narrow approach if owner review confirms every preserved selector is filtered through the same effective policy intersection as concrete child tools.

options.title: Move the fix to runtime materialization
options.body: Pause this branch and replace it with an owner-authored change closer to MCP/LSP materialization if inherited allowlists should stay concrete-only.

options.title: Wait for broader inheritance design
options.body: Keep the bug open but defer this PR if maintainers want the broader toolsAllow or strict-inheritance design to settle first.

recommendation.title: Refresh and accept selector preservation
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts against current main and land the existing narrow approach if owner review confirms every preserved selector is filtered through the same effective policy intersection as concrete child tools.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the delegated-session inherited restriction propagation path that this PR modifies.
